title: Hybrid quantization + batching strategy (draft)
body:
Purpose:
Draft proposal for a combined (hybrid) quantization + dynamic batching + cache-TTL strategy that balances token-cost improvements with tail-latency SLOs across typical Redwood workloads. This doc is intentionally experimental — contains rough numbers pulled from cost-model-v4 spreadsheet and notes-to-self about tradeoffs.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- Adopt hybrid quantization by default on non-sensitive customers for hosted tier: int8 for attention kernels + fp16 or bf16 for matmuls where accuracy shows risk. Keep full fp16 weights for enterprise/private unless explicitly approved.
- Use dynamic batching thresholds: small-chat (<= 64 token responses) default batch target = 8, medium-chat = 4, long-generation = 1 (no batching). Allow adaptive increase during low QPS windows up to 16.
- Cache policy: prefix caching for identical conversation prefixes with per-route TTLs: 10s for completion-heavy low-variability routes, 30s for slot-filling flows, 300s for embeddings/lookup routes. Stale-while-revalidate = enabled for cheap-model fallbacks.

Rationale / cost takeaways (from cost-model-v4 sheet):
- Hybrid-quant (int8 attentions + fp16 rest) reduces GPU memory footprint ~20% and token GPU time ~12% on A100/Trn-like kernels in our benchmarks. Rough hosted cost delta: ~18–27% per-token saving on short-chat workloads.
- Batching synergy: at batch target=8 we see an additional ~10–15% per-token reduction vs batch=1, but increase in p95 latency by ~30–50ms (numbers vary by model & sequence length).
- Caching is highest leverage for high-reuse routes: for an FAQ route with 40% prefix reuse, enabling caching cut per-request compute by ~55%.

Suggested default settings (prototype):
- Quantization profile:
  - hosted-default: hybrid-int8-attn + fp16-weights (flag: quant_profile=hybrid-v1).
  - dedicated/enterprise: quant_profile=off (admin opt-in).
  - private: quant_profile=off unless customer requests; provide an audit report.
- Batching policy:
  - route.categories: short-chat, medium-chat, long-chat, embeddings
  - short-chat: batch_target=8, max_batch_wait_ms=25, max_batch_size=16
  - medium-chat: batch_target=4, max_batch_wait_ms=30, max_batch_size=12
  - long-chat: batch_target=1 (disable batching)
  - embeddings: batch_target=32, max_batch_wait_ms=50, max_batch_size=128

- Cache TTL defaults:
  - short-chat (volatile): 10s
  - slot-fill / form flows (stable within session): 30s
  - embeddings/lookup (idempotent): 300s
  - fallback-model responses (cheap replica): SWR=60s

Example cost impact table (illustrative pulled from sheet):
- short-chat (avg resp 40 tokens, QPS steady 12): baseline cost $0.0126 / 1k tokens -> hybrid+batch -> $0.0094 (~25% savings).
- embedding batch (avg 1536 dims, batch 32): baseline $0.22 /k -> optimized pipeline w/ int8 quantized runtime -> $0.165 (~25% savings).

Quality regressions & guardrails:
- Run regression eval set (per-model & per-route) before enabling hybrid-int8 globally. Thresholds: ROUGE/EM/semantic-similarity drop <=1.5% absolute for chat; embeddings cosine drift <=0.02.
- Canary rollout: 1% accounts -> 5% -> 20% -> full. Monitor: gen-quality metrics, p95 latency, token-error-rate. Auto rollback if quality metric breach for 1 hour.

Experiments plan (next 6 weeks):
1) A/B test hybrid-int8-attn on hosted small-chat for non-PII demo orgs (sheet tab: "exp-hq-1"). Metrics: cost/k, p95 latency, semantic-sim score.
2) Run batch-size sweep (1,2,4,8,16) for 3 models (gpt-std-3, opt-ish-2, redwood-open-1) to map latency vs cost curve and find ops-safe batch targets.
3) Cache TTL tuning by route: target reducing compute by 30% with <5% freshness misses.

Rollout & Ops notes:
- Implementation: runtime flags + model artifact metadata (quant_profile tag). Serving-runtime to expose quant_profile in model manifest.
- Metric instrumentation: add per-request fields: quant_profile, batch_size_actual, cache_hit (bool), cache_ttl_applied. Wire these to datadog/console for 90-day retention during rollout.
- Ticket links: see linked_artifacts for RFC and experiment sheet. Create tickets: ENGINEERING-quant-2026 (runtime kernel selection), PRODUCT-OPT-451 (canary dashboard), SRE-cache-instrumentation.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What is legal/compliance posture for quantized models (export control / FIPS concerns)? Need legal check.
- Privacy: ensure quantization does not modify logging/audit formats.
- Should we allow hybrid-quant at model-version level (so model-v2 might be quant_profile=hybrid while v3 is off)? I think yes.

Action items (short):
- [Aisha] finalize experiment sheet and schedule runs (by 2026-03-17).
- [Miguel] add metric fields + skeleton dashboard (by 2026-03-12).
- [Ethan] prototype kernel selection shim and a small perf run on p4d (by 2026-03-24).
- [Claire] draft canary rollout doc + rollback criteria (by 2026-03-18).

Notes to self: keep this doc light and focused on tradeoffs. We should not overcommit to int8 for attention if customer QA flags any hallucination regressions. Keep rollout conservative.

End of draft.
